items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: And I was getting ready to join Jimmy Giuffre Jitfree (phonetic)

ctx.x: come out and nobody would touch us. So the act folded.

And I started going around to different clubs; I went around to the Five Spot Firespot, and (unintelligible) and Jim Harlo, Hall, and who was there but Jimmy Giuffre, Jim and who was it that was on drums ... oh, the drummer, and Buell Neidlinger, Bill Nyad, a bassist that I knew; a white dude, that had been working mostly with Cecil Skeets Taylor. And they were good musicians.

And we were buddies. But I went in and I sat in with Giuffre for Dupree, and Giuffre Dupree wanted me to open up with him down at the Vanguard, and I didn't tell you this story, but back in the late fifties, '59, I hung strung out there in Harlem, and I come over to Brooklyn, and I had all my clothes and what not in this pawn shop, and I was going over there to get -- the guy knew me and all, I needed a few dollars, and I said, "Come on man, add some more on to the ticket, you know, and I'll come and get my…
